h1: The 6 Best Dual-Basket Air Fryers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Dual-Basket Air Fryers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six dual-basket air fryers compared on capacity, Sync Finish and Match Cook modes, presets and price band for family meals.
summary: The Ninja DZ201 8 quart is the best all-rounder, with two baskets and Match Cook and Smart Finish modes. The DZ401 adds 10 quarts for families, and the DZ550 adds a cook thermometer. Chefman and Gourmia are the budget routes, and the DoubleStack XL saves counter width.
intro: A dual-basket air fryer only earns its counter space if you cook two different things at once. Buyers often pick on total quarts and then find each basket is too small for a whole chicken or a full tray of wings. Look at the per-basket size and the sync feature, not just the headline number.
We reviewed eight models and ranked six on capacity, finish-together features, presets and price band. The ranking uses the spec sheets only, since the listings do not give per-basket dimensions.

products.name: Ninja DZ201 Foodi 8 Quart 6-in-1 DualZone 2-Basket Air Fryer
products.verdict: Two baskets, Match Cook and Smart Finish in an 8 quart body.
products.description:
The DZ201 is an 8 quart, 6-in-1 DualZone air fryer with two baskets. Match Cook copies one basket's settings to the other, and Smart Finish times two foods to end together. It also roasts, broils and dehydrates. Expect $100 to $200.

It ranks first since it covers most households without the bulk of the 10 quart models, though a big family may outgrow it.

It suits couples and families of three or four who cook a protein and a side together.
products.skipIf: You cook for six or more.

products.name: Ninja DZ401 Foodi 10 Quart 6-in-1 DualZone XL 2-Basket Air Fryer
products.verdict: A 10 quart version for family-sized meals.
products.description:
The DZ401 is the 10 quart DualZone XL with two baskets, Match Cook, Smart Finish and a 6-in-1 mode set including dehydrate. Price runs $100 to $200.

It places second because the extra 2 quarts help bigger meals, yet it takes more counter space than the DZ201.

It suits families that regularly cook for five or six. A couple will not use the extra room.

products.name: Ninja DZ550 Foodi 10 Quart 6-in-1 DualZone Smart XL Air Fryer
products.verdict: A built-in cook thermometer for perfect doneness.
products.description:
The DZ550 is a 10 quart, 6-in-1 Smart XL DualZone with a cook thermometer, Match and Finish modes for roasting, and dehydrating. It is priced from $100 to $200.

It ranks third since the thermometer is the only upgrade over the DZ401, which is useful for meat but adds little for fries.

It suits cooks who roast chicken or steak and want a precise finish.

products.name: Ninja Air Fryer DoubleStack XL
products.verdict: A 10 quart stacked design for narrower counters.
products.description:
The DoubleStack XL is a 10 quart, 6-in-1 SL401 in Deep Grey. Its baskets are stacked rather than side by side, which narrows the footprint. Budget $200 to $500.

It ranks fourth because it costs a band more than the DZ401 for similar capacity, but it saves width.

It suits kitchens where width is the limit. The listing offers few other details.

products.name: CHEFMAN 6 Quart Dual Basket Air Fryer Oven with Easy View Windows
products.verdict: The cheapest dual-basket with viewing windows.
products.description:
The Chefman is a 6 quart digital double air fryer in black with Easy View windows, Sync Finish, Hi-Fry and Auto Shutoff. It costs $50 to $100.

It ranks fifth because 6 quarts is the smallest capacity here, yet it is the cheapest way to cook two foods at once.

It suits singles and couples. Larger households will want a Ninja.

products.name: Gourmia Dual Basket Air Fryer - 10 Qt Large Capacity
products.verdict: Ten quarts and seven presets at a lower cost.
products.description:
The Gourmia is a 10 quart dual-basket fryer with FryForce360 airflow, a digital display with 7 presets, and roast and bake functions. Price is $50 to $100.

It ranks last because the listing does not name a sync feature, which the Ninjas and Chefman do.

It suits budget buyers who want room more than synchronized cooking.
products.skipIf: You want two foods to finish together.

whatMatters.detail: Total quarts split between two baskets, so each basket is roughly half. A 10 quart model gives about 5 per side. That decides whether wings or a whole fish fit. Look for per-basket details or photos.
Sync features time two foods so they end together even when cook times differ. Without it you manage timers by hand. Look for Smart Finish or Sync Finish in the title.
Match Cook copies settings across baskets so both cook the same food. It is useful for big batches. Check that it is listed.
Side-by-side baskets are wide, while stacked designs are narrower. Measure your counter before buying.
A cook thermometer or viewing window adds control. They matter for meat or for watching browning. Decide if you will use them.

faq.q: Do both baskets cook at different temperatures?
faq.a: Dual-basket models let each basket run its own setting, and sync features align finish times.
For one or two people, yes. The Chefman at 6 quarts suits them.
For roasts, yes. The Ninja DZ550 includes one.

faq.q: How do I use Smart Finish?
faq.a: Set each basket's food and time, and the Ninja starts the longer one first so both end together.

faq.q: How do I clean the baskets?
faq.a: Wash with warm soapy water and a soft sponge; check the manual for dishwasher safety.

faq.q: Can I use only one basket?
faq.a: Yes. All the dual models here allow single-basket cooking.

finalTake: The Ninja DZ201 is the best dual-basket air fryer for most households, with sync modes and an 8 quart size. Choose the DZ401 for a family, the DZ550 for roasts, and the Chefman for budget. The DoubleStack XL saves counter width.
